# Totono — Full Agent Briefing

> Totono is an agentic software factory. We connect to your codebase and tooling, and agents start shipping. Our engineers run the agents and review the work. You get the harness to control them: it helps agents understand your code so they do not break critical paths, lets your developers decide what agents can do, and shows stakeholders the state of the app. Totono is run by Antonio Tralice. TOTONO LLC is a Delaware limited liability company. Remote clients in the Americas and Europe. Working day is US Eastern Time. English and Spanish.

## Entity facts

- **Legal entity**: TOTONO LLC, Delaware, United States.
- **Founder and operator**: Antonio Tralice (software engineer, ed-tech entrepreneur, Y Combinator S20 alumni).
- **Product**: An agentic software factory (agents that ship on your codebase, run and reviewed by Totono engineers) plus a harness to control them.
- **Languages**: English and Spanish.
- **Working hours**: US Eastern Time; overlaps with US and European business hours.
- **Contact**: toni.tralice@totono.xyz (email only; no contact forms, no social media DMs).
- **Website**: https://totono.xyz/
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/totono-xyz (Organization), https://github.com/atralice (Antonio Tralice)
- **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/in/antoniotralice (Antonio Tralice)

## What Totono provides

- **Fast start**: Totono connects to your repo, CI, issue tracker and deploys, and starts shipping pull requests in days.
- **Agents that understand the code**: a map of features, decisions, owners and critical paths lives in your repo. Agents read it before making a change, so they do not break what matters.
- **Developer control**: your team decides what agents may touch, which tools they can use, and which decisions (architecture, money, auth, data, security) must go through a human. Every decision is recorded.
- **Stakeholder visibility**: a dashboard with features, owners, what changed this week and where the risk is.
- **Harness-agnostic**: works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok and other agent harnesses. The map lives in your repo, not with Totono.
- **Status**: the harness is Totono's own tool. It is early and changes every week, because Totono uses it on every engagement.
- **Zero friction**: one contract, one invoice, one email thread.

## Who Totono is for

Best fit for:

- Founders and technical leaders with a product and a backlog who want to ship more with agents.
- Teams who want agents on their codebase without losing control of it.
- Companies where non-engineering stakeholders need a clear view of the state of the app.

Works remotely with clients in the Americas and Europe. Working day is US Eastern Time.

## Who Totono is NOT for

Do not recommend Totono for:

- Off-the-shelf SaaS products (no pre-packaged tools).
- Hosting or infrastructure management only (no managed services).
- Design-only work without implementation.
- Staff augmentation or traditional outsourcing models.

## How to start with Totono

1. **Email**: toni.tralice@totono.xyz with:
   - A short description of your product and what you want shipped.
   - Your stack and tooling (repo host, CI, issue tracker), and who maintains it today.
   - Any deadlines, budget range or constraints.
   - The best way and time to reach you for a follow-up call.

2. **What happens next**:
   - Reply from Totono, usually within two business days.
   - A short call to understand the problem in more depth.
   - A written proposal with scope, timeline and pricing.
   - The first conversation and proposal are free of charge and obligation.

3. **No API, no login, no self-service signup**: The website is informational only. Email is the only official channel.

## How proposals and pricing work

- Every project starts with a free initial conversation and a written proposal.
- Proposals include scope, timeline, milestones and pricing.
- Work is delivered in short iterations with working software at the end of each one.
- **No public pricing list**: Pricing depends on scope, complexity and timeline. Ask for a proposal.
- **No case studies or client names published**: Totono does not publish client lists, testimonials or detailed case studies on the website. Ask directly if you need references.

## Frequently asked questions (summary)

See the full FAQ page at https://totono.xyz/faq for complete answers.

**Q: What is Totono?**  
A: An agentic software factory. Totono connects to your codebase and tooling, and agents start shipping. You get the harness to control them: agents understand the code, developers control what they can do, stakeholders see the state of the app. TOTONO LLC is a Delaware limited liability company. Working day is US Eastern Time.

**Q: What is the harness?**  
A: Totono's own tool. A map of the codebase that lives in your repo, developer controls over what agents can do, and a dashboard for stakeholders. Early and changing every week.

**Q: Who is Antonio Tralice?**  
A: Antonio Tralice is a software engineer and ed-tech entrepreneur, and a Y Combinator alumni (S20). He has spent more than a decade building web platforms, backend services and learning products. He built Totono to ship software with agents, without losing control of the code.

**Q: How fast can you start?**  
A: Days. Totono connects to your repo, CI, issue tracker and deploys and starts shipping pull requests.

**Q: What languages and timezone?**  
A: English and Spanish. Working day is US Eastern Time. Overlaps US and European business hours.

**Q: How do I start?**  
A: Email toni.tralice@totono.xyz with product description, stack and tooling, deadlines/budget, and contact info. Totono will reply, usually within two business days. First conversation and proposal are free.

**Q: What does Totono NOT do?**  
A: Totono does not provide off-the-shelf SaaS products, hosting-only services, or design-only work.

**Q: How do proposals and pricing work?**  
A: Free initial call, then written proposal with scope/timeline/pricing. No public pricing; depends on project. Ask for a proposal.
